text:
emma.design: quick design check — the routing pill in the alert preview looks too similar to the suppression pill. users might toggle the wrong one when skimming. screenshot: https://img.redwood.local/preview.png
raj.prod: agreed. visual weight is almost identical. suggest: add a small icon for routing vs suppress, and reduce the fill for suppression to an outline.
maria.eng: outline could be tricky for low-contrast themes. if we do outline, we need a >=3:1 contrast with background or add a subtle left border color.
aiden.sre: also thinking about keyboard nav — when you tab through the preview stack, the focus ring currently lands behind the pill instead of on it. keyboard users will miss the affordance.
emma.design: good catch. focus should land on the interactive element. propose: focusable role for each pill with `tabindex=0` and visible 3px outline.
joaquin: small nit on copy: the pill says "Routing" and the tooltip says "Route to channel" — maybe unify to "Route" / "Route to" inconsistency.
sam.writer: +1 unify. also change tooltip to active-voice: "Routes alerts to selected channel" instead of passive.
raj.prod: aside: the suppression preview currently shows an inline toast anchored to bottom-left of the preview pane. on narrow screens it covers the action buttons. can we anchor to top-right of the preview or make it non-modal?
emma.design: I tried top-right and it felt disconnected from the pill. idea: attach a small inline banner directly above the pill group (like a compact callout) so it reads as contextual feedback.
maria.eng: implementation note — inline banner should be in DOM order right after the pill container to preserve screenreader reading. also add `role=status` and `aria-live=polite` so VO announces changes but doesn't interrupt.
aiden.sre: for regressions, please avoid `aria-live=assertive`. we had a bug where floody metric changes spammed the screen reader.
designbot: accessibility check: suggested text for banner: "Suppression active — alerts will be silenced for 2 hours." (length <= 80 chars). Also recommend `aria-hidden=false` only when visible.
joaquin: on hover state there's a preview of which channels are affected. can we include a compact keyboard-accessible list that opens with Space/Enter? currently list requires mouse to see channel badges.
emma.design: yes — make the preview expandable with `aria-expanded` and ensure all badges are focusable links. fallback should be a visually-hidden summary for screen readers like "Suppression affects 3 channels: #ops, #pager, #alerts".
sam.writer: microcopy suggestion for empty threshold state: current text "No thresholds set" feels cold. try: "No alert thresholds yet — set one to get notified when SLOs slip." include a CTA button "Add threshold".
raj.prod: love that. and add a small help link: "How to pick thresholds" linking to docs.
maria.eng: edge case: if user creates a threshold then immediately enables suppression, we need the preview to reflect combined behavior. right now preview shows them independently which is confusing.
aiden.sre: I can make the backend return a merged-preview object: preview_state = computePreview(thresholds, suppressions, routing). then frontend just renders a single canonical preview.
emma.design: perfect — that will reduce mismatch. one more accessibility ask: when the preview changes due to live edits, add a subtle motion (100ms fade) but also offer a reduced-motion class to respect user prefs.
joaquin: animation + reduced-motion ✅. last small layout ask: breadcrumb above the threshold list is long and pushes the preview down on small viewports. consider collapsing breadcrumbs into a single "alerts > service > thresholds" compact pill with overflow menu.
emma.design: will mock that. thanks everyone — I'll update the spec and post a new frame. tagging @maria.eng @aiden.sre for follow-up on DOM order and merged preview contract.
maria.eng: got it — I'll draft the API shape today.
aiden.sre: I'll add tests for screenreader announcements and keyboard focus in the QA checklist.
sam.writer: I'll iterate microcopy and send a content PR.
designbot: note recorded: design-review: routing/suppression pill contrast, keyboard focus, aria-live rules, merged-preview API, toast anchor -> inline banner, empty state CTA.
emma.design: thanks all. small follow-up: can someone run a quick color-blindness check on the updated pills (deuteranopia)? I can drop palettes into Figma.
raj.prod: i'll run the check this afternoon and paste results. :white_check_mark:
